title: The Choice That Could Be Reversed
fact_notes: 人物・町・行事・数値や結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A student named Aki was asked to choose a design for the cover of her school's annual magazine.
sentences.ja: アキという生徒は学校の年刊誌の表紙デザインを選ぶよう頼まれた。

sentences.en: She received two excellent proposals from classmates and found it surprisingly difficult to choose between them.
sentences.ja: クラスメートから優れた提案を二つ受け取り、そのどちらかを選ぶのが驚くほど難しいと感じた。

sentences.en: For several days, she examined both designs without making any progress toward a final decision.
sentences.ja: 数日間、両方のデザインを検討したが、最終決定には近づかなかった。

sentences.en: She was afraid that selecting one design would prevent the other from ever being considered again.
sentences.ja: 一方を選ぶともう一方を二度と検討できなくなるのではないかと恐れた。

sentences.en: Her teacher suggested distinguishing between a temporary choice and a decision that could not easily be reversed.
sentences.ja: 教師は一時的な選択と簡単には取り消せない決定を区別するよう提案した。

sentences.en: The magazine had not yet been sent to the printing company, so there was still time to experiment.
sentences.ja: 雑誌はまだ印刷会社に送られていなかったので、試す時間は残っていた。

sentences.en: Aki could place each design on a sample cover without making a permanent commitment to either one.
sentences.ja: アキはどちらかに最終決定せずとも、それぞれのデザインを見本の表紙に配置できた。

sentences.en: This suggestion made the problem seem less threatening because the early choice would have limited consequences.
sentences.ja: 最初の選択の影響は限られているため、提案によって問題はさほど恐ろしくないものに思えた。

sentences.en: Aki prepared two digital samples and invited a small group of students to look at them briefly.
sentences.ja: アキはデジタル見本を二つ作り、少人数の生徒に短時間見てもらった。

sentences.en: She asked which title was easier to recognize and which picture communicated the subject more clearly.
sentences.ja: どちらが題名を認識しやすく、どちらの絵が主題を明確に伝えるか尋ねた。

sentences.en: Rather than simply collecting votes, she wrote down the explanations that accompanied each student's preference.
sentences.ja: 単に票を集めるのではなく、各生徒の好みに伴う説明を書き留めた。

sentences.en: Several readers identified a useful feature that she had previously failed to notice.
sentences.ja: 数人の読者は彼女が以前気づかなかった有用な特徴を指摘した。

sentences.en: After reviewing the comments, Aki selected one design and suggested a minor adjustment to its title.
sentences.ja: 意見を見直した後、一つを選び、題名の小さな修正を提案した。

sentences.en: She explained her reasons to both classmates and obtained permission before changing the selected design.
sentences.ja: 両方のクラスメートに理由を説明し、選んだデザインを変える前に許可を得た。

sentences.en: Only after everyone had checked the final sample did she send the magazine to the printer.
sentences.ja: 全員が最終見本を確認してから初めて、雑誌を印刷業者に送った。

sentences.en: She felt more confident because the earlier trial had given her information unavailable at the beginning.
sentences.ja: 最初には得られなかった情報を試行によって得たので、より自信が持てた。

sentences.en: The experience taught Aki that not all decisions require the same level of caution from the beginning.
sentences.ja: この経験から、すべての決定が最初から同じ程度の慎重さを必要とするわけではないと学んだ。

sentences.en: An inexpensive and reversible trial can sometimes reduce uncertainty without creating a serious new risk.
sentences.ja: 低費用でやり直せる試行は重大な新たなリスクを生まずに不確実性を減らせる場合がある。

sentences.en: However, a decision with lasting consequences may require more careful preparation before any action is taken.
sentences.ja: しかし長く影響する決定は、行動を起こす前により慎重な準備が必要なこともある。

sentences.en: Aki learned to ask not only which choice was better but also when a choice needed to become final.
sentences.ja: アキはどの選択が良いかだけでなく、いつ最終決定する必要があるかも問うようになった。

a conclusion about what to do

questions.prompt: Why did Aki find the original decision difficult?
options: The magazine had already been printed.
Her teacher had forbidden her to choose.
questions.explanation_ja: 優れた提案が二つあった。

questions.prompt: What did Aki fear about choosing one design?
options: Both proposals would be withdrawn by the teacher.
The other might never be considered again.
The printing company would choose a different school.
questions.explanation_ja: 一方を選ぶと他方を検討できないと恐れた。

questions.prompt: What distinction did the teacher make?
questions.explanation_ja: やり直せる選択と取り消しにくい決定。

questions.prompt: Why could Aki try both designs?
options: The printer had finished both versions.
She had already obtained a final contract.
Both designs had been permanently rejected.
The magazine had not been sent to the printer.
questions.explanation_ja: まだ印刷に出していなかった。

questions.prompt: What did she ask readers to judge?
options: Title recognition and clarity of the picture.
The amount of paper in the printer.
The cost of the annual magazine.
questions.explanation_ja: 題名の見やすさと絵の伝わりやすさ。

questions.prompt: What did she collect besides votes?
questions.explanation_ja: 好みの理由を記録した。

questions.prompt: What did Aki obtain before adjusting the selected design?
Why did she feel more confident?
options: All future decisions had become risk-free.
The trial provided information she had lacked earlier.
She had avoided hearing other people's comments.
The printer guaranteed the magazine would be perfect.
questions.explanation_ja: 試行で新しい判断材料を得た。
取り消して戻せるという意味。

options: Match the timing and caution of a decision to how easily it can be reversed.
Every decision should be made immediately.
All decisions should be delayed until there is no uncertainty.
Testing an idea makes a final decision unnecessary.
questions.explanation_ja: 取り消し可能性に応じて決め方を変える。

grammar.focus: would prevent the other from ever being considered
grammar.explanation_ja: prevent A from -ingはAが〜するのを妨げる。

grammar.focus: that could not easily be reversed
grammar.explanation_ja: 関係代名詞thatがdecisionを修飾し、受動態になっている。
rather thanは選ばなかった行動を示す。

grammar.focus: Only after everyone had checked the final sample did she send
grammar.explanation_ja: Only afterが文頭に出るため主節は倒置。

discourse.role_ja: まだ印刷前であり試行できることを示す。
投票だけに頼らない方法への転換。
意見確認後の行動を示す。
やり直せる決定と長期的な影響がある決定を対比。

paraphrases.source: She was afraid that selecting one design would prevent the other from ever being considered again.
paraphrases.rewrite: She worried that choosing one proposal would end any future consideration of the other.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 選ばなかった案を再検討できなくなると心配した。

paraphrases.source: Her teacher suggested distinguishing between a temporary choice and a decision that could not easily be reversed.
paraphrases.rewrite: Her teacher proposed separating provisional choices from decisions that were hard to undo.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 仮の選択と取り消しにくい決定を区別した。

paraphrases.source: Rather than simply collecting votes, she wrote down the explanations that accompanied each student's preference.
paraphrases.rewrite: Instead of only counting preferences, she recorded the reasons each reader gave.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 票だけでなく理由も記録した。

paraphrases.source: Only after everyone had checked the final sample did she send the magazine to the printer.
paraphrases.rewrite: She waited until everyone had reviewed the final example before sending it to the printer.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 全員の確認後に印刷へ回した。

cloze.explanation_ja: 一時的な選択と取り消しにくい選択。
票だけでなく理由を集めた。
長く続く影響には慎重な準備が必要。
